segments.text: Hello Daniel, come in, have a seat.
Would you like to start today?
In general, she just said I come.
She said I look exhausted and she's right, I am.
What does exhausted look like for you?
Like I'm running on fumes. I work as a project manager at a logistics company and I've been completely burnt out since October.
Since October? Did something happen then?
Not one thing. We lost a big client. Half of the team got moved onto the rescue plan.
So I ended up doing three people's jobs. Just never came back after that.
Not working day
Got to my desk by 7 and I'm still answering messages at 10 that night
Even when I'm not working I'm thinking about work
That's a very long day, how was your sleep?
terrible
Most nights I sleep about four hours
I wake up at 3 and fall back asleep
My head is stirred
Shipping schedules
decline
Whether I've forgotten something
Then I look at the clock and I do the math on how little sleep I'm gonna get, which makes
it worse.
Then I lie until about 5 and get up and make tea.
It's very dreading you know, if I'm honest.
Sounds draining.
Is there anything else going on?
Yeah, my father. He was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease in the autumn.
What to carry alongside everything else? How is he?
Still himself, mostly. His hands shake. He's slower. He gets frustrated.
He's always been the strong one.
How are you involved in his case?
Who drives him to the hospital and leads?
The biology appointments are every few weeks.
It's about an hour each way.
Is there anybody who shares that with you?
Not really.
My younger sister Hannah lives in Toronto, so all the care for our father falls on me.
How do you feel about it?
Guilty for even saying it.
She calls him every Sunday.
She's not the one who's neglecting him.
Just I'm the one who's hearing.
about it. He feels selfish to be tired when he's the one who leaves the cell. So anything
to anyone? To Hanafida? She asks how I am, I say fine. What would be the point? She can't
do anything from Canada.
You want her to know if you said it.
That I'm not fine?
That some days they sit in a car park at the hospital for 10 minutes before they go in?
Cause they can't face it?
It's an important thing to notice.
What happens in those ten minutes?
Nothing really.
I just breathe.
Look at our people going in.
Everybody looks tired here.
You mentioned your GP.
She had blood tests.
She said it's stress and exhaustion if I ask to talk about talking to someone.
She said I had a good time.
Did your girlfriend look dead, to be honest?
She said she was done watching me disappear.
She is very patient, she makes me tea and doesn't push me to talk.
But I can see she is worrying about her too.
In what way?
She stopped asking if I want to go away for the weekend because I always said no.
That's the thing I feel worst about actually.
What stops you from saying yes?
The emails come back to 200 of them.
And that might mean something.
So even rest has a price?
Yeah, exactly.
Can't remember the last time I was properly off.
duty for yourself before october you ran i call me tears every saturday morning
we've done it for six years and now i stopped about two months ago my legs feel like blood
I just never went back.
How do you feel about it?
I think I've lost a part of myself.
It was the one time in the week nobody could reach me.
What would it mean to get some of that back?
A lot, probably.
I just can't picture the time that would come from.
Leave this for a moment.
What is your relationship with your boss like?
Pearson.
He's alright as a person, but he sends emails at 11 at night
I didn't expect an answer before breakfast.
What did you want one rice?
I don't eat it. Every time. Even if I'm on a bed.
I hate it.
What are you afraid would happen if you didn't answer?
I think I wasn't committed. There's a restructuring this spring and I'm afraid they'll let me go.
And if they did?
I think part of me would be relieved. I'd feel horrible about being relieved. I have a mortgage.
Both things can be true.
Suppose so.
I never said that I would talk.
Apart from the third man.
Unirritable.
He slapped a colleague last week or in nothing and went and sat in the toilet for ten minutes.
What was happening for you in those minutes?
Hurry was going and my hands were shaking.
You thought for a second it was a heart attack but it passed.
Has it happened before?
Couple of times.
Once on a train to Manchester.
Just to get off and stand on a platform.
That sounds frightening.
It was. I hadn't told anyone about it. Not even Claire.
Thank you for telling me. What are you afraid means?
That I'm losing it. That I'm gonna end up like, I don't know, coping.
Have you noticed anything that makes it worse?
Coffee, probably.
I want about six cups a day.
And I've started having wine in the evenings to switch my head off.
Two glasses, sometimes three.
How do you feel about the phone?
Easy.
It works for an hour.
It's free anyway.
I know it's not helping.
You're noticing that clearly.
That is useful.
It doesn't feel useful.
Feels like I'm listing everything that's wrong with me.
I hear a person who has been holding a great deal on his own for a long time.
What was it like to say it today?
Strange.
Bit of relief actually.
Like putting on a bag, but I didn't realise I was carrying.
What do you carry when you would like to boot down first?
The nights, I think.
If I could sleep, I could probably cope with the rest.
We can start there. Did anything about your family growing up shape how you handled this?
My grandfather worked in the mines near Yorkshire. He never complained about anything. Not once.
That's the same. Just get on with it.
I keep thinking he would think I was weak for being here.
If he were here.
Then I'm not weak. Just very tired.
That sounds like something you'd do yourself as well.
Not yet.
It's fine. You don't have to.
About what we could do between.
Would you people like to try something?
Small. Can't get much left.
Very small. For 20 minutes.
Beards.
What would actually happen?
I think probably you wouldn't even notice.
Would you try it?
Yeah, half past nine, perhaps.
I could make it a thing with Claire.
Tea on the sofa.
That sounds good.
And a note of how the night goes?
I can do that.
I'm afraid when I wake up, if I wake up.
We're nearly out of time. How are you feeling?
Dark, lighter. It's normal to feel a bit shaky after saying all that.
Barely normal. It takes energy to say it loud and low.
Thank you. I think I needed to hear that.
Same time next week?
Yeah, I'll be here.
I'll try to make it on time. The trains are awful.
